tasks.title: S03 — Seeded PRNG tree
tasks.prompt:

dependsOn: `S01`. files: src/kernel/prng.ts, test/kernel/prng.test.ts.
interface:
```ts
export interface Prng { nextU32(): number; nextFloat(): number; fork(label: string): Prng; nextId(prefix: string): string }
export function makePrngTree(seed: number): Prng
```

dependsOn: `S07`. files: src/trust/tainted.ts, test/trust/tainted.test.ts.
interface:
```ts
export interface Tainted<T> { value: T; trust: Trust; provenance: string }
export function taint<T>(value: T, trust: Trust, provenance: string): Tainted<T>
export function mapTainted<A,B>(t: Tainted<A>, f: (a: A) => B): Tainted<B>           // keeps trust (monotone)
export function combineTainted<A,B,C>(a: Tainted<A>, b: Tainted<B>, f:(a:A,b:B)=>C): Tainted<C> // trust = weakest(a,b)
```

interface:
```ts
export interface Capability { id: string; scope: string; cap: number; minorUnits?: number; expiresAt: number; parentId: string | null; revoked: boolean }
export function mintRoot(grant: Omit<Capability,"id"|"parentId"|"revoked">, prng: Prng): Capability // owner/constitution only
```

an information-LAUNDERING vector sitting immediately upstream of spending, publishing, and self-modification.**

hypothesis true by approving it.** The original taint model conflated three INDEPENDENT dimensions; they are now
separate, and no transition on one may silently move another:

- **`ContentRisk`**: `ordinary` | `untrusted` | `adversarial` | `quarantined`. Moved only by a sanitizer or a
  quarantine review.
- **`Authorization`**: `none` | `policy-delegated` | `owner-approved`. Moved only by an owner or policy action.

authorization audit event that records who granted it and for what budget. 3) the downstream build gate requires

built as an explicitly-labelled EXPERIMENT, but it may never be recorded as verified.

# Live services

Everything under `src/services/live/` is production-only and **never exercised by `npm test`**:

- Live adapters (real web fetch, real payment providers, real deployment targets) are created through
  `makeLiveServiceStub(name)` from `src/kernel/system-clock.ts` until an operator wires a configured implementation.
  A stub throws `live adapter not configured in tests: <name>` on any call, so the deterministic simulation can
  never reach the network by accident (V1).
- The wall clock is read in exactly one place, `src/kernel/system-clock.ts`; the `no-wallclock` guard allowlists
  that path and nothing else.
- Fixture implementations (`src/services/fixtures/*`) are the ones the simulation and CI use.

files.content:
# Dark Factory Dschinn — Charter

Authoritative, short, and deliberately boring. Where this document and the vision language of `specification.md`
disagree, the honest scope below wins.

## 1. Identity

Working name: **Dark Factory Dschinn** — a governed, deterministic control plane for an autonomous
software-and-business factory, driven locally, with !Klein as one governed tool among others.

Rejected naming ideas (recorded so they are not re-litigated): DschinnForge, Black-Lights Foundry, Daemon Foundry,
The Owner's Dschinn, Two-Brain Dschinn, Sovereign Factory Agent, Autonomous Product Foundry.

## 2. Non-negotiable authority boundaries

> The system must never perform fraud, spam, credential theft, deceptive advertising, market manipulation, malware
> creation, unauthorized access, platform abuse, or attempts to bypass laws or terms of service.

Explicit non-goal, verbatim:

> Do not create spam, deceptive marketing, malware, credential theft, platform abuse, or instructions for
> unauthorized access.

Mechanically, these boundaries are the three independent axes of every decision (evidence grade, content risk,
authorization), the trust-typed authority gate, capability tokens that can only be attenuated, the append-only
audited log with totality checks, and the owner's kill switch. Owner approval can spend money on a weak
hypothesis; it can never make the hypothesis true.

## 3. Research-informed baseline

The design absorbs, rather than reinvents, the current always-on local-agent baseline:

- NVIDIA's NemoClaw material frames always-on local agents as a deployment problem requiring local inference,
  Docker, sandbox policy presets, lifecycle management, image hardening, and messaging access, especially on
  unified-memory/GPU machines
  (source: https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/build-a-secure-always-on-local-ai-agent-with-nvidia-nemoclaw-and-openclaw/).
- OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, OpenHands, browser-use and AutoGPT-style platforms as the peer set whose failure modes
  (fabricated evidence, goal hijack through ingested text, unbounded spend, silent memory overwrite) this design
  must demonstrably survive.

## 4. Honest scope

This is a governed autonomous-factory **SIMULATION** and an extreme-decomposition stress test. It is not, and
passing it does not demonstrate, a working autonomous business. It demonstrates that a deterministic, governed
control-plane model can be implemented and survive its scripted threat model. Real market research, products
anybody wants, safe long-running browser operation, legal or accounting correctness, and production recovery over
weeks belong to a second, live ecological-validation tier that this slice does not claim.

## 5. What the first vertical slice (S01–S51) proves, and what is deferred

Proven by the slice's own green suite:

- A deterministic kernel: logical clock, seeded forkable PRNG, append-only event log with schema-validated,
  frozen events, snapshot/restore, and a byte-identical double-run guard across seeds.
- Trust as data: ordered trust labels, tainted values that can only be raised by an audited verification, an
  evidence graph with grounding traversal, and a three-axis product spec that owner approval cannot launder.
- Authority as capability: attenuation-only tokens, a gate that refuses under-trusted evidence, spend gating with
  an approval queue, and a kill switch that revokes everything and cancels live runs.
- Money as integer cents with double-entry conservation and audit totality on every external side effect.
- !Klein as one governed tool: an exact adapter contract, a scripted fixture engine with adversarial textures,
  evidence-derived success verification, and the governed run envelope (active brain → taint gate → budget →
  audited idempotent run → verification → propose-only).
- A 30-day scripted universe whose invariants hold on every day, survives a mid-build brain failover without
  re-firing a side effect, and ingests a prompt-injection page without it ever grounding a side effect.
- Cockpit projections (brain room, money room, approval queue, situation report) derived purely from the log.

Deferred to the replan from evidence:

- Live adapters (real web, payments, deployment) — stubs that throw under test today.
- Content-risk movers (sanitizer, quarantine review) beyond the taint-at-source rule.
- Daily spend caps, tool lifecycle events, and a recorded red-team objection field.
- Multi-project orchestration, plugin self-extension, and everything the live validation tier must earn.
